messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 tail latency breach detected for /v1/generate (streaming) on redwood-3b, region=us-west-2. p95=420ms -> 1.1s, p99=1.8s -> 6.8s. Streaming stalls and partial responses observed. Paging oncall @oncall-alex. Triggered by recent LB rollout 'lb-policy-v2' at 03:20 UTC.

oncall-alex: I'm on it — joining. Seeing same numbers on Grafana: p95 ~430ms, p99 ~6.7s, 5xx +0.12%. Streaming stalls increased ~20% over baseline, sessions dropping mid-stream.

sre-jin: Quick triage: router logs show misroute churn post-rollout. ~12% of requests now hitting shard-47 (hot partition) which historically handles <2% of traffic. Queue depth and CPU for shard-47 spiking. Suspect weight skew from policy change.

eng-runtime-lead: Confirmed — the lb-policy-v2 change adjusted prefer-local weights to favor same-az shards; in some shards that created a hot partition (shard-47) due to uneven shard key distribution. Immediate plan: 1) reduce routing weight to shard-47 2) mark shard-47 draining 3) enable eager fallback to nearby shard pool.

netops-maya: I can push weight delta now. Applying weight shard-47 -> 0.2 (was 1.0) and enabling eager-fallback flag. Will monitor.

metrics-bot: Query results: shard-47 cpu=92%, queues=~3k, kv-cache misses +5x, streaming stall count +250 over 5m. Global p99 reduced slightly in the last 30s sample.

oncall-alex: Netops change applied (weight -> 0.2). Watching metrics.

sre-jin: After weight change (T+40s) sampled p99 dropped to ~1.2s on aggregate, p95 stable. Streaming stalls fell from 20% -> 6% in first 3 mins but not back to baseline. Looks like KV cache thrash caused residual stalls.

eng-runtime-lead: To prevent immediate re-hotting, mark shard-47 draining and shift new sessions away. Command I will run now: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routers/mark_shard_draining -d '{"shard":"shard-47","reason":"hot_partition_misroute","ttl_seconds":1800}' 
```
Also rolling back lb-policy-v2 to previous config (lb-policy-v1) for canary groups.

netops-maya: Draining cmd acknowledged by controlplane. Starting rollback of lb-policy-v2 for us-west-2 canary.

product-csm: Customer impact: CS triage showing ~4 customers reporting streaming gaps (some partial output, some repeated reconnects). Opening CS ticket CS-3241 and notifying account teams for high-touch customers.

support-oliver: Workaround for app teams: enable client-side retry with exponential backoff for streaming stalls and/or pin to a known stable model variant (redwood-3b-quant) where available. Documenting steps in support playbook.

oncall-alex: Handoff plan: I will remain oncall for 2 hours to monitor. If p99 remains >3s or stalls >10% for >10m, we escalate to eng-runtime-lead and trigger full page. Incident doc: creating INC-2026-0423-RTR-01.

sre-jin: Root-cause hypothesis: lb-policy-v2 altered weight distribution -> hot partitioning of shard keys -> overloaded shard -> KV cache cold miss cascade -> streaming stalls. Actions to close: 1) rollback policy rollout 2) drain and rebalance shard-47 3) run a shard heatmap job to detect skewed key distributions 4) add preflight checks for future weight rollouts.

eng-runtime-lead: Follow-ups I've assigned: add guard to rollout tool to detect >5% skew to any shard, add retry+backoff recommendation to streaming SDK, and create an automated draining action we can trigger via controlplane.

product-csm: Communicated to affected customers and set expectation for an incident postmortem.

support-oliver: Logging KB note with commands and temporary mitigations; will post in #support and link to CS ticket.

oncall-alex: Monitoring shows p99 now ~980ms, stalls ~3.4% and trending down. Keeping oncall status. If stable for 30m we can move to monitoring-only.

metrics-bot: Snapshot @ T+45m: p95=380ms, p99=940ms, streaming stalls=2.9%, shard-47 cpu=45%, queue=~300.

sre-jin: Leaving follow-ups: run replay of traffic to validate rebalancing, tighten canary thresholds for LB rollouts, schedule postmortem in 24h.

eng-runtime-lead: Thanks everyone. Adding note: avoid prefer-local weight bumps without heatmap check. I'll lead the postmortem.

oncall-alex: Closing live mitigation thread, switching to incident doc for root cause and action items. If anything new emerges ping me directly. :thumbsup:
